observation.visible_scene: A wide, static overhead-ish view of a light wood floor covered with an elaborate pattern of multicolored dominoes arranged in loops, arcs and lines. A black slanted ramp/track held up by a yellow pedestal sits in the middle, with a row of colored dominoes lying flat along its top surface. The lower and central loops (yellow, blue, purple, orange, magenta, green) and the ramp remain still throughout.
visible_changes: The scene is static for the first ~0.24 s; then a white-topped domino in the small blue loop at the upper right tips over (around t=0.28–0.36 s).

A leftward sequential cascade then propagates along the top arc of the layout: the white-topped domino of the green loop (~t=0.52–0.64 s), then of the next blue loop (~t=0.68–0.84 s), then of the yellow loop (~t=0.92–1.08 s), then of the purple loop (~t=1.20–1.40 s), and finally the white-topped domino of the leftmost green loop begins to tip near the end (~t=1.52–1.60 s).
Each toppling is a single upright domino rotating to lie flat within its loop; the rest of each loop stays standing, so the change is local rotation, not bulk translation or deformation.
The camera does not move (floor grain and all uninvolved loops hold identical positions); the only motion is the dominoes tipping.
outside_clip_unknowns: No hand, projectile or other visible trigger causes the first toppling within this excerpt; the initiating contact is unseen.
Whether the cascade continues past the left edge of the frame after t=1.60 s is not shown.
The eventual fate of the still-standing dominoes (including those on the black ramp and the lower loops) is outside the clip.
uncertain_details: Exact inter-group contact points that link each loop into one chain are not visually confirmable; the right-to-left order is inferred from the timing of successive topplings.
A pink cluster near the upper right may or may not be part of the same cascade; its change is ambiguous.
Precise frame times for each tip-over are approximate given the 0.04 s sampling.
